title: Config Sheriff: automated decisioning, KV-prefix quarantine, and rollback playbook
creator: Priya Raman
description: Design and implement an automated decisioning layer (Config Sheriff) that monitors config changes affecting batching/caching and triggers guarded rollback or quarantine actions. The feature should reduce cost-related regressions caused by misconfigured batching/cache settings, provide an automated 'pause-and-inspect' quarantine for affected KV prefixes, and produce deterministic reconciliation steps to recover to a safe state.
background: We repeatedly see config rollouts (batching window, prefetch keys, cache TTLs) that cause transient cost spikes or token-regressions. Current manual rollback processes are slow and imprecise and often miss KV cache contamination. This ticket centralizes decision logic, safety thresholds, and a state reconciliation playbook that protects production while allowing rapid remediation.
proposal: Introduce a 'Sheriff' microservice that subscribes to config events and telemetry streams and evaluates scoped rollback policies.

Implement KV-prefix quarantine: when a config delta triggers a safety condition, the sheriff marks affected KV prefixes 'quarantined' and routes new requests to a clean prefix while preserving read-only fallback for warm-up.
Define composite triggers that combine cost, latency, error rate, and cache-hit regressions with hysteresis to avoid flapping.

Support three automated actions: WARN (notify and snapshot state), PAUSE (stop rollout and isolate prefixes), AUTO-ROLLBACK (revert config and start reconciliation), with manual approval gates configurable per project tier.
Add a simulation harness to run 'shadow applies' against historical traffic to estimate rollback impact before executing live actions.
acceptance_criteria: Sheriff service deployed behind feature flag and can subscribe to config-change stream.
At least two composite triggers implemented and tested: cost-per-token delta > 35% sustained for 5 minutes, and cache-hit-rate drop > 20% with P95 latency degradation > 30%.
KV-prefix quarantine implemented: quarantined prefixes receive read-fallback and new writes go to a new prefix namespace.
Automated rollback flow reverts config and creates a reconciliation job that rehydrates safe prefixes and validates metrics return to baseline within defined SLOs.
End-to-end integration test and canary run shows zero false positive auto-rollbacks on historical non-regression window.
Playbook documentation added in Confluence and linked in the ticket.

telemetry: metrics: cost_per_token (USD/token) - compare baseline vs post-change
latency P50/P95/P99 per route and per-model
rollout_health_score: composite metric used by Sheriff to summarize impact
decision_audit_log: trace-id tagged events for each Sheriff decision
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Feature flag off: deploy Sheriff and telemetry collectors (smoke tests)
Phase 1 - Observe: enable decision engine in WARN-only mode for 48 hours against low-risk projects
Phase 2 - Shadow-actions: run PAUSE/AUTO-ROLLBACK decisions in dry-run mode and validate outcomes against simulation harness
Phase 3 - Canary: enable automated PAUSE (manual approve before AUTO-ROLLBACK) for 5% of rollouts across staging traffic
Phase 4 - Gradual: increase to 25% then 100% project coverage with AUTO-ROLLBACK enabled for P0/P1 incidents only
Phase 5 - Post-launch: quarterly policy reviews and threshold tuning based on false-positive/negative metrics
risks: False positives triggering unnecessary rollbacks causing availability regressions
Quarantine may lead to cache cold starts and transient latency spikes if not warmed properly
Policy complexity could be hard to reason about across many projects leading to misconfigurations
Security concerns around automated config writes and KMS access for rollback operations
Operational burden of maintaining simulation harness and keeping traffic replay fidelity
